newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's Telecel sees higher '97 profit.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Telecel sees higher '97 profit.

text.p: Portuguese mobile phone operator Telecel expects to post a higher profit in 1997 than in 1996, its president Antonio Carrapatoso said on Wednesday.
"We are confident that if market conditions continue to be favourable profits will be higher in 1997 than in 1996," Carrapatoso told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
Telecel today announced a 1996 net profit of 7.3 billion escudos, up 199 percent on the previous year.
Carrapatoso said he expected that Telecel would issue good dividends for 1997.
"With the results of 1997 and our forecasts for investment, it should be possible, with the approval of shareholders, to issue good dividends for 1997," Carrapatoso said.
Telecel has issued no dividends so far. Some 40 percent of the company was floated last December.
Telecel and its rival TMN, a unit of Portugal Telecom, control the Portuguese cellular phone market.
Telecel does not expect to announce a capital increase soon as it had sufficient cash flow from its business to finance its activities, Carrapatoso said.
"In principle we don't foresee in the short term the need to raise any more capital," he said.
"Given the investment levels that we foresee for the business, we think that the cash flow that is going to be generated by this business will be enough," he added.
Telecel said it spent 14.8 billion escudos on investment in 1996, 31 percent more than in 1995.

Carrapatoso said it was premature for Telecel to consider entering the fixed telecommunications market, due to be liberalised by 2000, and for now the company would focus its activities on the cellular market.
